quote: If more of us valued food and cheer and song above hoarded gold, it would be a merrier world.
source: J. R. R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, chapter XVIII, The Return Journey (George Allen and Unwin, 1937) (Thorin Oakenshield)
speaker: Thorin Oakenshield

evidence.where: The full text of chapter 18, The Return Journey, read online, with Thorin's dying speech to Bilbo intact; the chapter title and number confirmed against Tolkien Gateway's chapter listing for The Hobbit. One search result claimed the sentence belongs only to the 1977 television adaptation; the chapter text refutes that, and the adaptation's wording is different.
evidence.edition: The Hobbit, or There and Back Again (George Allen and Unwin, London, 1937)
evidence.locator: chapter XVIII, The Return Journey, in Thorin's last speech

reason: The wording is exact and the sentence sits in Thorin's dying speech, between Some courage and some wisdom, blended in measure and But sad or merry, I must leave it now. One caution for the editor and not for the citation: shipped.js puts Tolkien at two for the year, so this line takes him to the cap of three and closes out the three Tolkien carry-ins, one of which, small hands do them because they must, is marked for September as well.
